[Jan 2038]

The Dutch are proud to present their new [Piet Hein Class](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/_TCT3-umOtk/hqdefault.jpg) Stealth guided missile destroyer.

Combining knowledge with the USA, both countries aimed for a next generation version of [the Zumwalt class program](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=68opxApU3N4). The Piet Hein-class destroyers are a class of Dutch Royal Navy guided missile destroyers designed as multiple-mission stealth ships with a focus on land attack. The class is multi-role and designed for surface warfare, anti-aircraft warfare, and naval gunfire support. They can fulfill the place of battleships in naval fire support.

The [Piet Hein class](http://i330.photobucket.com/albums/l434/Raevyn_bucket/AltCGX.png) has a low radar profile; an integrated power system, which can send electricity to the electric drive motors or weapons, total ship computing environment infrastructure, serving as the ship's primary LAN and as the hardware-independent platform for all of the ship's software ensembles; automated fire-fighting systems and automated piping rupture isolation.

[The destroyer](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1d/DD%28X%29.png) carries 25 × MK 57 VLS modules, with a total of 150 launch cells and is able to launch a multitude of missiles. Two 155 mm/62 caliber Advanced Gun Systems makes it hit hard with conventional ordinance and 4 Goalkeepers Gen2 make for excellent close range missile, aircraft and vessels defense. It has a wave-piercing tumblehome hull whose sides slope inward above the waterline and is improved with Visby stealth technology. This will reduce the radar cross-section, returning much less energy than a conventional flare hull form.

The lead ship is named HNLMS ["Piet Hein"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piet_Pieterszoon_Hein) named after the legendary admiral and folk hero who captured the Spanish treasure fleet in 1628.
